head.text: Load-Use Hazard — worst-case 5-cycle ID stall (stage 7e: IF/ID/RR/EX1/EX2/MEM1/MEM1B/MEM2/WB)

foot.text: L is fetched at tick 0 and advances one stage per cycle, IF through WB. C is fetched one cycle behind L (tick 1) and decodes at tick 2, where it sees L's rd still live in the pipe (RR) — load_use goes high and stays high for ticks 2-7 (kronos_hazard priority 3a: stalls pc/if_id/id_rr, bubbles into RR) because the load occupies six producer slots and the only load-forwarding path, FWD_MEMWB (mem_wb_q.alu_result, registered), isn't valid until L reaches WB at tick 8. C is stalled in ID for tick 2's normal cycle plus 5 more (ticks 3-7) before advancing to RR at tick 8 — the worst-case 5-cycle stall (§7). Measured at stage 7e (bench_load_use_hit, §11): 7 cycles/op end-to-end (load issue + the 5-cycle stall + the consumer's own execute), consistent with this diagram. The Timing Table's pre-7e figure of 3 cycles (5-stage-pipeline era) is what this re-measurement replaces.
